title: McQuillan's Bridge rehabilitation approved after heritage and cost debate
subtitle: Downtown parking and transit mitigation funding, overnight shelter review, energy equity plan, audited financial statements and community grants.
overview: Council approved the environmental assessment for McQuillan's Bridge, directing staff to rehabilitate and strengthen the heritage-designated structure rather than replace it {{vote:m18}}. Supporters pointed to heritage protection and the risk of legal delays. Opponents said the cost was too high.

Council also agreed to put up to $25,000 of downtown construction mitigation money toward transit and/or parking measures on Wyndham Street. Council asked the Downtown Guelph Business Association to match it. Staff said this could mean other mitigation actions are not delivered unless the budget is topped up {{vote:m14}}. Council asked the County of Wellington to share its review of overnight shelter entry processes and barriers {{vote:m11}}. City Hall will no longer serve as an overnight warming centre.

Council approved the 2025 consolidated financial statements and audit findings report {{vote:m10}}. It received the Energy Equity Action Plan {{vote:m16}} and approved Community Investment Strategy recommendations {{vote:m17}}. Through the consent report, it appointed a closed meeting investigator, approved an updated Procurement By-law taking effect September 1, 2026, and approved a new Outside Water Use By-law and a new building permit fee structure.

decisions.detail: Council approved the assessment and directed staff to issue a Notice of Completion to rehabilitate and strengthen the bridge {{vote:m18}}.

Council approved up to $25,000 from the construction mitigation budget for transit and/or parking measures on Wyndham Street, requested matching funds from the DGBA, and asked for a DGBA update on its own efforts.

Council asked the County of Wellington to share its review of shelter entry processes, provide a 24/7 phone line, consider data collection on refusals, and make any changes before the 2026-2027 winter program.
Council approved the 2025 Consolidated Financial Statements and External Audit Findings Report.
Council received the plan, directed staff to determine resourcing needs through the multi-year budget, and asked that energy efficiency be evaluated in the affordable housing RFP.
Council approved the update's recommendations, with future grant streams and inflation adjustments subject to future budget updates.
Council approved a new building permit fee structure, a revised reserve fund target and automatic fee indexing from 2028.
Council approved the updated Procurement By-law, effective September 1, 2026.

debate: On McQuillan's Bridge, delegates urged rehabilitation, citing the bridge's heritage designations and its irreplaceable value. One delegate suggested a lighter pedestrian loading standard might lower costs. Staff said the standard could be reviewed during detailed design.

Supporters of rehabilitation said a replacement could face heritage legal challenges. Staff estimated this could cost at least a year and possibly more, plus potential legal fees. Opponents said rehabilitation cost too much when a replacement was estimated at much less, and that councillors only saw detailed costs recently.

On downtown mitigation, a delegate favoured transit incentives over parking, and another worried about setting a precedent for other construction areas. Council added transit to the motion. Staff said free parking or transit must be designed so it brings customers downtown. One councillor said downtown businesses see parking as their top concern.

On the overnight shelter, delegates described barriers to shelter entry and asked for a clear threshold for opening warming centres. Staff said City Hall was unsafe and not suited to overnight use, and that the County is the shelter service provider. Councillors said there is no public data on refusals.
On the audit, one councillor asked whether the results affect the City's AAA credit rating. The auditor said credit ratings are outside the audit's scope.
